🔥🇲🇽 <u>UIF and SAT Open Files on Every Morena Candidate for Governor</u>

On presidential instructions, Mexico's Financial Intelligence Unit and the SAT opened files on all Morena coordinators aiming for the 17 governorships in 2027. Investigators are checking their assets, properties and bank accounts, along with those of spouses and adult children, so that dirty money from corruption or organized crime doesn't fund campaigns. Contralínea's Miguel Badillo reports that one of the files belongs to Santiago Nieto, the former UIF chief and now Morena's coordinator in Querétaro. Lines of inquiry in his case include links to invoice mills (EFOS) and alleged illicit enrichment.
banner: UIF AUDITS ALL MORENA GOVERNOR HOPEFULS

🇲🇽📈 <u>Japan's JCR Holds Mexico at A-, Stable</u>

Japan Credit Rating Agency ratified Mexico's long-term foreign-currency sovereign rating at A- and its local-currency rating at A+, both with a stable outlook. JCR credits the export-driven industrial base, a narrowing deficit backed by spending restraint and stronger tax collection, and debt it calls moderate next to similarly rated countries. About 80% of that debt is held by the domestic market. It projects ~1.5% growth in 2026 and ~2% in 2027, driven by consumption and Plan México investment.

🇲🇽🇵🇸 <u>Mérida Tells Israeli Companies: Not Our Water</u>

About 700 people marched in Mérida demanding that Yucatán break ties with Israel, after Israel Trade & Investment and six Israeli firms took part in Pro Agro Innovación 2026, a fair promoted by Governor Joaquín Díaz Mena's administration. Maya communities and collectives want the agreements on water and agriculture made public and cancelled, warning about the peninsula's aquifers. Israel's ambassador Yoed Magen defended the companies, citing a 2021 letter of intent signed by PAN governor Mauricio Vila. "Son genocidas," the marchers chanted.
banner: MÉRIDA MARCHES: ISRAEL OUT OF OUR WATER

🇲🇽🇧🇷 <u>Mexico Shuts Its Door to Brazilian Poultry Over Newcastle Outbreak</u>

Mexico's Agriculture Ministry, through Senasica, suspended imports of chicken meat, poultry byproducts and fertile eggs from Brazil after Brasília confirmed Newcastle disease on a commercial broiler farm in Nova Itaberaba, Santa Catarina. The ban covers commercial shipments and anything tourists carry in their luggage. It is the second suspension in a year and a half.

🇲🇽🕯️ <u>Day of the Dead to Move 53 Billion Pesos</u>

Concanaco-Servytur estimates that spending on Day of the Dead celebrations from Oct. 25 to Nov. 2 will reach 53 billion pesos. That is up 7% from 49.5 billion in 2025 and 45.3 billion in 2024. The money flows to cempasúchil growers, pan de muerto bakers, candle and altar sellers, public markets, restaurants, hotels and transport, as reported by El Economista.

🇲🇽🗳️ <u>2027 Midterms Poll: Morena 46%, PAN 8%, PRI 6%</u>

El Financiero's national poll for the June 2027 Chamber of Deputies election puts Morena at 46%, the PAN at 8%, the PRI at 6% and MC at 5%, with 31% undecided. Morena alone more than doubles the entire opposition combined (19%), and 55% of respondents have a favorable opinion of it. The poll interviewed 800 people between Sept. 10 and 20 (margin of error ±3.5%), and it comes from a business paper that is no friend of the 4T.

🇲🇽🏛️ <u>Brugada: Settle Petty Theft With Repair, Not Case Files</u>

Mexico City Mayor Clara Brugada sent the city Congress a reform to the Civic Culture Law. Under it, non-violent thefts and property damage worth up to 50 UMA (5,865.50 pesos) could be resolved through civic justice: return of the goods, repair of the damage, community service or administrative arrest. This applies only to first offenses, and only if the victim agrees. The criminal route stays open. "It's not about punishing less, but about resolving better."
banner: CDMX: CIVIC JUSTICE FOR PETTY THEFT

🇲🇽⚖️ <u>Supreme Court Upholds AMLO's Science Law: Public Research First</u>

Mexico's Supreme Court voted 7–1 to uphold the 2023 General Law on Humanities, Sciences, Technologies and Innovation, which opposition minorities in Congress had challenged. Public institutions keep priority in research funding. Researchers at private universities can still receive SNII stipends if they work with public institutions, for example by teaching, and focus on national priority areas set by Secihti. The lone dissent came from Justice Loretta Ortiz, who argued that the value of research is decided by "peers, not a secretariat, not an entity of the State."

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Inside Mexico's Congress, Israel Named "Friendly Embassy of the Year"</u>

At the PRI's invitation, the evangelical group Policías Celestiales A.C. took over the Chamber of Deputies' Salón Legisladores to hand out its "Seguridad con Valor 2026" awards, organized with backing from Israel's embassy. Press attaché Dahlia Neumann collected the "friendly diplomatic mission of the year" prize on behalf of Ambassador Yoed Magen. The "mayors of the year": PAN's Giovanni Gutiérrez (Coyoacán) and Mauricio Tabe (Miguel Hidalgo), and PRI's David Sánchez Isidoro (Coacalco). The same day, people in Yucatán marched to demand an end to relations with Israel.
banner: PRIAN HONORS ISRAEL'S EMBASSY IN CONGRESS

🇲🇽🛢️ <u>Pemex Takes Back the Pump: 91% of Wholesale Gasoline</u>

Pemex's share of Mexico's wholesale gasoline market jumped from 79% to 91% so far this year, according to PetroIntelligence data reported by La Jornada. In diesel it holds 82%. The reason is price: in 2026, private resellers charged gas stations 4.86 pesos more per liter of regular, 1.11 more for premium and 2.07 more for diesel. The 2013 energy reform promised that competition would bring cheaper fuel. Instead, the public company is the cheap option.
